column2: If the eleventh and twelfth fall at the remainder of the night and the thirteenth follows, the merit is of the twelfth and the breaking of the fast is on the thirteenth.
If the eleventh is present only as a digit on the twelfth day, and the twelfth is either present or absent on the thirteenth,
then even the eleventh so joined: the earlier is for householders, the later to be taken by ascetics and by those without male descendants.
If the full eleventh is pure and nothing of the twelfth exists on it, and the twelfth is on the thirteenth, how is it decided?
Here the earlier tithi is for householders and the later for ascetics; some devotees say it is the second that should be fasted.
When the eleventh is not found joined with the twelfth, and the twelfth is also on the thirteenth, others hold the same...
the pure twelfth is to be fasted by all, without doubt; some say the earlier, but that view is not right.
On a transit day (sankranti), on a Sunday, and at an eclipse, a householder with sons should not break a fast or begin one.
On Sunday, on a parva night, on the fourteenth and eighth by day, a man who eats on the eleventh day-and-night should perform the Chandrayana.
When a solar eclipse occurs, one should not eat in the first three watches; if he eats, he is equal to a drinker of liquor.
If an eclipse of the moon or sun occurs in the middle of the anvadhana or ishti rite, the sacrificers should perform expiation, O best of sages.
At a lunar eclipse he should offer with the verse "Soma" in the tenth, and with the verse "Apyayasva", and "Somapa", O Brahmin.
At a solar eclipse he should offer with "Ud u tyam jatavedasam" and "Asatya" — three mantras are cited.
The wise one who, having settled the tithi by the path of Smriti, keeps vows and the like gains imperishable fruit.
Dharma is what the Veda enjoins; Keshava is pleased by dharmas. Therefore those devoted to dharma go to the supreme abode of Vishnu.
Those who wish to practise dharma have the form of Krishna himself; the disease of worldly existence never troubles them.
One who unknowingly has gone to his mother or her co-wife should himself cut off his own testicles, proclaiming his sin,
and holding them in his hand, go toward the south-west; on the road he should never consider pleasure or pain.
He who goes, not looking behind, until death is purified; or he may throw himself down from a height, declaring the sin.
For going without discrimination to a woman of his own class or a higher class, he should attentively perform the Brahmin-slayer's vow for twelve years.
One who by repeated habit but unintentionally goes to a woman of his own or a higher class is purified, O best of twice-born, by burning in a fire of dried dung.
If he turns back from his mother before the discharge of semen, he should perform the Brahmin-slayer's vow; if after discharge, death by fire.
If he stops before discharge with women of his own or higher class, he should perform the Brahmin-slayer's vow for nine years, devoted to Vishnu.
With a Vaishya woman or his father's wife he should keep the vow six years; having gone to a Shudra woman or his teacher's wife, three years.
If, infatuated by desire, he goes to his maternal aunt, paternal aunt, teacher's wife, father-in-law's wife, uncle's wife, maternal uncle's wife, or his daughter,
he should perform the Brahmin-slayer's vow properly on two days; if many times in a single day, for three years.
If once, he is purified by a vow of a year; if over three days, he is purified only by burning in fire, not otherwise.
One who goes by desire to a Chandali, a Pukkasi, a daughter-in-law, a sister, a friend's wife or a disciple's wife,
should keep the Brahmin-slayer's vow for six years, O lord of sages; if unintentionally, the year-long Krichchhra.
Expiation is declared for association with great sinners; one purified by expiation obtains the fruit of all rites.
With whichever of the four, beginning with the Brahmin-slayer, one associates, by performing that vow he is purified, without doubt.
One who unknowingly associates with them for five nights should perform the Kayakrichchhra properly; otherwise he falls.
For association of twelve days, the Mahasantapana is declared; after association of half a month, fasting twelve days.
The Parakas for association of a month; for three months, the Chandrayana; having associated six months, two Chandrayanas.
For association of slightly less than a year, a six-month vow; this is said threefold if done knowingly, in order.
Having killed a frog, mongoose, crow, boar, mouse, cat, goat, sheep, dog or cock,
a Brahmin should do half a Krichchhra; the Atikrichchhra for a horse; the Taptakrichchhra for killing an elephant; the Paraka for killing a cow.
For killing a cow intentionally, the wise see no purification. For things such as drink, bed, seat, flowers, roots and fruit,
and for theft of food and eatables, purification is by the five cow-products. For dry wood, grass, trees and jaggery,
and for leather, cloth and meat, three days' fasting. Having killed a lapwing, ruddy goose, swan, karandava,
owl, crane, pigeon, water-fowl, parrot, chasha, heron, porpoise or tortoise,
one should fast twelve days; for eating semen, faeces or urine, he should keep the Prajapatya vow.
Three Chandrayanas are declared for eating a Shudra's leavings. A menstruating woman, a Chandala, a great sinner,
a woman in childbirth, an outcaste, leavings, a washerman and the like — having touched them one should bathe with clothes on and taste ghee,
and the pure-minded, O Brahmin, should chant the Gayatri a hundred and eight times. If one touches any of these unknowingly or eats after,
he is purified in three nights, by fasting and the five cow-products, O Brahmin. In bathing, giving, chanting, and in eating, O Narada,
one who hears or speaks the word of any of these should vomit the food eaten, bathe and fast;
on the second day, having tasted ghee, he becomes pure, O Narada. If in the middle of a vow one hears even the sound of one of these,
he should chant the mother of the Vedas (Gayatri) a thousand and eight times. Of sins, the greatest is reviling Brahmins and gods;
no atonement for it is seen in any scripture, O Narada. Those said by the wise to be equal to great sins —
their expiation should be done thus by rule. One who performs expiations devoted to Narayana
has his sins destroyed; otherwise he falls. One who is free of passion and the like, filled with remorse,
full of compassion for all beings, devoted to remembering Vishnu, whether joined with great sins or all sins,
is to be known as already freed from sins, since he is devoted to Vishnu. The man who remembers Narayana, without beginning or end, of universal form, faultless,
is freed from ten million sins. Remembered, worshipped, meditated on or bowed to,
Vishnu, who goes into the hearts of the good, destroys sins. Whoever worships Hari even by chance contact or through delusion
is freed from all sins and goes to Hari's abode. By a single remembrance of Vishnu the mass of troubles is destroyed;
for him, O Brahmin, the attainment of heavenly and other enjoyments is to be inferred. A human birth, hard to get, is gained by those, O lord of sages,
and even then devotion to Hari is declared hard to attain. Therefore, having obtained this human birth, hard to get and fleeting as lightning,
one should worship Hari with devotion, who frees from the bonds of the bound animal; all obstacles vanish and purity of mind arises,
and one gains supreme liberation when Janardana is worshipped. The aims of life — dharma, wealth, desire and liberation — are eternal;
for those devoted to worship of Hari they are accomplished, without doubt. Having obtained this human life, running after sons, wives, house, fields, wealth and grain,
O fools, do not be proud. Abandoning desire, anger, greed, delusion and pride,
slander of others and blame, worship Hari with devotion. Leaving all business, worship Janardana.
The trees of Yama's city are seen near. As long as death does not come, as long as old age does not come,
as long as the senses are not impaired, so long worship Hari. The wise should not trust this perishable body.
Death is always near; wealth is extremely fickle; the body is close to death; therefore give up pride.
Unions end in separation; everything is perishable in a moment. Knowing this, O fortunate one, worship Janardana.
One is troubled by hope; liberation is extremely hard to get. One who worships Vishnu with devotion, though a great sinner,
also goes to the highest place, from which he does not grieve. All holy places, sacrifices and the Vedas with their limbs, O good one,
do not equal a sixteenth part of the worship of Narayana. What use are Vedas, sacrifices, scriptures, or visits to holy places,
what use are austerities and vows to those without devotion to Vishnu?
Those who worship Vishnu of infinite form, having seen him in an image, the best, known by Vedanta, physician for the disease of worldly existence — those mortals go to Achyuta's abode.
Remembering the beginningless Self of infinite power, the support of the world, the one praised by the gods, light by nature, supreme, called Achyuta, a man comes to a friend.
Greater than these is to be known the one who is always devoted to meditation; therefore with all effort the collection of dharma should be made.
